question: How soon can ovulation return after an abortion procedure?

options.A: Only when the first normal period ends

explanation: Ovulation often resumes very quickly after pregnancy termination, sometimes within two weeks, meaning a new pregnancy is possible before normal menstruation returns. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h1)

question: What is the main risk of delaying contraceptive counseling until the first post-procedure menstrual period?

options.A: An increased risk of an unintended repeat pregnancy
options.B: Immediate surgical complications from the abortion
options.C: Total loss of hormonal control in the body
options.D: Permanent damage to the ovarian lining

explanation: Because ovulation happens before the first period, waiting until menstruation returns leaves the client unprotected during the fertile window. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h1)

question: What does client-centered contraceptive counseling prioritize above all else?

options.A: The personal reproductive goals and choices of the client
options.B: The hospital policy on family planning targets
options.C: The nurse's personal preference for birth control methods
options.D: The fastest and cheapest method available in the clinic

explanation: Client-centered care centers entirely on the individual's needs, preferences, and life circumstances rather than outside pressures. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h2)

question: Why must a nurse review a client's medical history before recommending a hormonal contraceptive?

options.A: To check if the client has ever had a routine dental cleaning
options.B: To determine how many children the client currently has at home
options.C: To screen for conditions that could make specific methods unsafe
options.D: To calculate the exact cost of the prescription for the pharmacy

explanation: Certain medical conditions, such as high blood pressure or blood clotting disorders, make specific hormonal methods dangerous to use. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h2)

question: What does immediate contraceptive initiation mean in post-abortion care?

options.A: Starting pills only when the client feels severe pelvic pain
options.B: Starting the method before the client leaves the clinic after the procedure
options.C: Waiting for three normal menstrual cycles before starting any method
options.D: Using barrier methods only after the follow-up appointment next month

explanation: Immediate initiation provides protection right away while the client is still at the healthcare facility, reducing the risk of an unremembered follow-up. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h3)

question: A client is discharged after an abortion without a birth control method and fails to return for her two-week checkup. What major risk does she face?

options.A: A permanent inability to ever produce estrogen again
options.B: An unintended repeat pregnancy due to early ovulation
options.C: Severe weight loss from sudden hormonal withdrawal
options.D: An automatic infection in the uterine lining

explanation: Missing the follow-up without a started method leaves a gap in protection during a time when fertility has already returned. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h3)

question: Which of the following is an example of a long-acting reversible contraceptive method?

options.B: A packet of daily oral contraceptive pills
options.D: Male latex condoms used during intercourse

explanation: Implants and intrauterine devices are classified as LARC methods because they work continuously for years without daily action from the user. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h4)

question: Why are LARC methods considered very effective for post-abortion contraception?

options.A: They completely stop all bacteria from entering the reproductive tract
options.B: They do not require daily action or memory from the user to prevent pregnancy
options.C: They destroy all male sperm cells before they reach the vagina
options.D: They can only be removed permanently by surgical removal of the uterus

explanation: Human error, like forgetting a pill, is a major cause of contraceptive failure, which LARC methods bypass entirely. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h4)

question: What is a major clinical advantage of barrier methods compared to hormonal contraceptives?

options.A: They provide protection against sexually transmitted infections
options.B: They guarantee a 100 percent prevention rate against pregnancy
options.C: They alter the body's natural hormone levels permanently
options.D: They last for five continuous years without replacement

explanation: Condoms and other barriers block physical contact and infectious fluids, something hormonal birth control cannot do. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h5)

question: Which factor most often decreases the effectiveness of short-acting hormonal methods like oral contraceptive pills?

options.A: Inconsistent daily use or missed doses by the client
options.B: The time of day the client eats her meals
options.C: The client's natural blood pressure levels
options.D: Using the pills during the winter months

explanation: Short-acting methods depend heavily on the user remembering to take or apply them on a strict schedule every day. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h5)

question: How should a nurse respond when a client expresses fear that an IUD will cause permanent infertility?

options.A: Tell the client that her fears are irrational and insist she accepts the device anyway
options.B: Provide calm, evidence-based education explaining that fertility returns immediately upon IUD removal
options.C: Agree that permanent damage is common and suggest she avoids all birth control
options.D: Ignore the comment and document that the client refused all medical advice

explanation: Respectful nursing care involves correcting myths gently with factual information while supporting the client's ultimate autonomy. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a true fact about modern post-abortion contraceptive use?

options.A: Ovulation returns within two weeks for many women after an abortion
options.B: Barrier methods protect against common sexually transmitted infections
options.C: Contraceptives cause permanent damage to a woman's reproductive organs
options.D: Intrauterine devices can be inserted safely right after a procedure

explanation: Standard reversible contraceptives do not cause permanent organ damage; fertility recovers once the method is stopped or removed. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h6)

question: What critical warning signs should a nurse teach a post-abortion client before she leaves the clinic?

options.A: Slight breast tenderness in the morning
options.B: Severe pelvic pain, heavy bleeding, or high fever
options.C: A temporary change in her favorite foods
options.D: Mild fatigue and slight spotting for two days

explanation: These symptoms are red flags that can indicate infection, retained tissue, or other complications requiring immediate medical evaluation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h7)

question: Why is proper documentation of contraceptive counseling important in the client's health record?

options.A: It stops the client from ever changing her birth control method later
options.B: It proves to the hospital management that the nurse worked full hours
options.C: It guarantees that the healthcare facility will receive extra government funding
options.D: It ensures continuity of care and creates a legal record of the client's informed choices

explanation: Clear records allow other healthcare providers to know what method was chosen, what education was given, and what follow-up is needed. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h7)
